analysis.title: GS - Tkach - October FOMC Goldman's Take from Traders and Research - 27 Oct 2026
key_insights: The Fed is expected to hold at this week's October FOMC. GS Trading says a hike is effectively off the table given dovish Fed-speak since September, the midterms and growing AI-capex downside risk. The focus is on how Warsh squares a hold with his 'timelier return to 2%' messaging after a hot October CPI, with a December hike still largely priced.

GS US Economics reads FOMC participant comments as pointing to a compromise of raising the funds rate every other meeting. That means a skip in October and a likely second hike in December. They do not expect significant new information from the press conference.

GS US Economics thinks the FOMC might modify its statement to adapt Vice Chair Jefferson's language: 'Any further adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate to support a timelier return to the Committee's 2 percent goal will depend on trends in the data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks.'

The Fed's hawkish pivot has raised interest rates and moderately tightened broad financial conditions since September. GS Economics says this is only a bit more than is usually associated with one hike and much less than the four hikes now priced. The FOMC is therefore unlikely to see it as excessive or as a replacement for hikes.

If the FOMC keeps an every-other-meeting pace in 2027, it could consider a hike in March. GS Economics does not expect one, because it expects inflation to improve as tariff, energy shock and AI price pressures fade. Growth or employment concerns would also likely end the hikes. A more extreme and long-lasting energy shock raises the risk of a larger 'January effect' in inflation as firms pass on costs with start-of-year price increases.
GS baseline and probability-weighted Fed forecasts are considerably less hawkish than market pricing, because GS is skeptical the FOMC will hike four times and expects cuts down the road.

Rates desk (Short Macro Trading) views the 3bp of hike premium priced for October as a function of price action into the July FOMC, not a credible chance of a hike. It cites uniformly dovish communication since September, the meeting's proximity to the midterms, and growing downside risk from AI capex. It calls the probability of a hike 'nothing short of unfathomable'.

The September dot plot is described as likely intact, with only one voting dot (Williams, lower) remarked over the past month. Warsh opened his September press conference by stressing hikes in delivering 'a timelier return to the Committee's 2% goal', and how he threads that against a hold after the hot CPI 'remains a mystery'. The desk expects a hawkish hold.

With December priced at 23bp cumulative, the Short Macro desk sees little room for error and puts little weight on the tail of a 50bp hike. It estimates consensus positioning as short 2x z6 vs long 1x z7, on the view that Trump will re-escalate in the Middle East once the midterms pass. It sees the most painful quadrant for most participants as an 'SVB-esque' torque steepener led by the front contract if the AI drawdown worsens sharply.

The Short Macro desk suggests micro-flattener expressions, paid Dec/Jan vs received Mar/Apr from 9bp in each jump, as cheap convexity for the modal scenario of a tapering hiking cycle as inflation normalizes into Q2 of next year.

Government Trading sees a rangebound rates market. It expects the 10-year Treasury to trade 4.80-5.30% and finds it challenging for yields to rally beyond that. It likes buying dips and steepeners into flattening moves. A resolution of the Middle East conflict is the catalyst that could drive a bigger rally.

On positioning, CTAs remain short duration and hedge funds are light after unwinding sizeable long-duration positions, mostly in Europe and less so in the US. Real money moved from underweight to less underweight duration and bought a touch more after CPI.

GS Rates Strategy says market pricing through mid-2027 is roughly aligned with an every-other-meeting pace, so the Committee's relative emphasis on inflation versus financial conditions will shape front-end stickiness. Belly longs typically do relatively better through hikes and their aftermath. Valuation asymmetry has moderated, but positioning for belly outperformance remains a sensible bullish-leaning expression.

Midterm elections are a potential source of post-FOMC volatility. GS Rates Strategy expects the initial rates reaction to depend on perceived medium-term implications for AI regulation and Iran developments. A shift in risks around the AI investment trajectory would likely dominate as a driver of duration.

FX: options price a 45bp gap for the FOMC, which looks rich versus historical meetings. Owning ATM vol is hard to justify unless Warsh makes a hawkish slip-up. USD skew is relatively cheap, and front-end GBPUSD risk reversals look like attractive protection for a hawkish Fed outcome.

FX spot: central bank meetings, month-end flows and a marginally better risk backdrop favor selective USD strength. The desk thinks EUR stays heavy, with scope to retest the previous low of 1.1113. BOJ risk is a more dovish message than the market expects, but any USDJPY rally after it is an opportunity to sell USD. The desk would sell USDCAD ahead of a BOC it thinks can sound hawkish.

Equities: October saw a large TMT pullback and a meaningful VIX vol event. Vol has performed on larger downside moves, tails remain extremely firm and hedging demand is strong. The AI growth narrative turned more bearish after credit concerns over neocloud funding, specifically the CRWV selloff, which makes this week's big tech earnings particularly important.

Index vols and skew are at historically elevated levels on a YTD lookback, with catalysts in the election, tech earnings and FOMC. SPX is chopping around its 50-day moving average and the bulk of dealer long gamma sits to the topside. Index Derivs Trading thinks options are the best way to play these events.

Index Derivs Trading trade ideas: for a selloff, SPX 6Nov 7200/7550 put spread at $29.5 (ref 7720f) given steep skew. For a rally, outright SPX 6Nov 7750 calls at $50.3 (ref 7720f), which the desk considers cheap enough to own outright.

Macro Research (Vickie Chang) expects a hold and a December hike. With a December hike almost fully priced and nearly two more after that, the bar for Warsh to sound hawkish relative to pricing is high. Clearing FOMC and big tech earnings may set up a locally friendlier patch for risk assets, as it has for the last two meetings. The desk wants that upside in protected form because of oil escalation, midterm and AI-sentiment risks.
Macro Research suggests USD shorts in options form, given lower FX implied vols, could give exposure to the Fed meeting if it is perceived as more dovish.

Credit: with no hike priced and the rates rally holding, the desk favors CDX HY over CDX IG locally as a tactical compression trade. Lower yields ease pressure on the weakest balance sheets and give IG AI-capex names another chance at primary issuance.

CDX IG was insulated on the way wider by gamma into this week's expiry. With most of that rolling off, it is exposed to continued volatility in IG AI CDS and European weakness on the Main/IG pair. A benign FOMC and stabilizing rates and vol would help CDX HY, supported by US core long real money demand.

Commodities: oil rallied sharply to six-month highs as the market repriced odds of a more violent new wave of US and Israeli attacks on Iran, possibly before the midterms. Iran threatened retaliation against energy and economic assets across the Gulf. The back end of the crude curve outperformed the front on longer-term disruption risk, while physical markets were balanced in October on large AG exports through STS.

Crude vol: front vol and call skew found a bid after months of selling off to below pre-war levels. The best performer in vol is deferred vol in cal27, supported by spec call and put demand and producer put hedging.
